text: Matt Pocock Skills for DSH 是面向 DSH 的工程与效率技能插件，通过向 ctx.skills 注册 provider，将技能目录中的 SKILL.md 按需载入，并提供相对资源基址以解析技能引用。技能集涵盖代码评审、需求与规格澄清、测试驱动开发、领域建模、调试诊断、研究和原型设计等工作流；部分技能可由模型调用，部分保留为用户显式调用。适合希望在 DSH agent 中复用结构化软件工程流程的开发者。无需额外 API 密钥或外部账号。

Matt Pocock Skills for DSH makes engineering workflows available to DSH agents through an on-demand skill provider. Its skills cover code review, specification shaping, TDD, domain modeling, bug diagnosis, research, and prototyping. No API key or external account is required.

Matt Pocock Skills for DSH 的功能「双轴代码评审」：依据用户给出的固定点比较当前改动，从代码规范和需求规格两个角度分别审查，并并列汇报结果。通过 code-review 技能触发。
Matt Pocock Skills for DSH 的功能「测试驱动开发指导」：提供 red-green-refactor 流程、测试边界选择和测试反模式指导，帮助 agent 通过公共接口验证行为。通过 tdd 技能触发。
Matt Pocock Skills for DSH 的功能「疑难问题诊断」：为难复现 bug 或性能回归构建紧密的反馈循环，并从测试、HTTP 请求、命令行或轨迹重放等途径寻找信号。通过 diagnosing-bugs 技能触发。
Matt Pocock Skills for DSH 的功能「设计原型验证」：按问题类型选择逻辑或 UI 分支，生成一次性原型来探索状态模型、业务逻辑或界面变化。通过 prototype 技能触发。
mattpocock-skills-dsh README · mattpocock-skills-dsh：[Matt Pocock](https://www.aihero.dev)'s engineering and productivity agent skills, packaged as a plugin for the **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**.

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · mattpocock-skills-dsh：27 skills — grilling, spec and ticket flows, TDD, code review, domain modelling, and more — installed as one bundle. The skill bodies are **verbatim** from upstream [`mattpocock/skills`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) v1.3.2. Only the packaging is new: a Cordis plugin that registers a skill provider on `ctx.skills`, so every agent preset in a profile sees these skills.
mattpocock-skills-dsh README · mattpocock-skills-dsh：The skills are "plug-and-play, not vibe coding": small, composable, and meant to be edited. Fork them and make them your own.

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Install：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:zhikedan/mattpocock-skills-dsh
```

Restart the Harness afterwards — a profile bundle is read at boot, so the skills appear in the next process, not the running one.

From a local checkout instead of GitHub:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add E:\path\to\mattpocock-skills-dsh
```

Remove it again:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove mattpocock-skills-dsh
```

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · What you get：27 skills. `model + user` means the agent may reach for the skill on its own; `user only` means it is invoked by you, because upstream marks those flows `disable-model-invocation: true` — a prescribed sequence that should not fire by itself.

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · What you get：| Skill | Invocation | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ask-matt` | user only | Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo. |
| `code-review` | model + user | Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X". |
| `codebase-design` | model + user | Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary. |
| `diagnosing-bugs` | model + user | Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow. |
| `domain-modeling` | model + user | B

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Layout：```
package.json        bundle manifest — dsh.bundle.patch is what makes this a DSH bundle
dsh.plugin.json     plugin identity, engine range, and the contributed skill names
cordis.patch.yml    inserts the provider row into the host plane
lib/index.js        the Cordis plugin: skill provider protocol over skills/

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Layout：The provider scans `skills/` one level deep, reads each `SKILL.md`'s YAML frontmatter for `name` and `description`, and loads the body only when a skill is actually requested. Each skill advertises a directory `resourceBase`, so a relative reference inside a body — [tests.md](skills/tdd/tests.md), `scripts/hitl-loop.template.sh` — resolves for the reader.
mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Upstream fidelity：Bodies are byte-for-byte upstream; nothing is translated or rewritten. Four deliberate packaging differences:

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Upstream fidelity：1. **Flat skill directories.** Upstream groups skills into `skills/engineering/…` and `skills/productivity/…`. This package ships `skills/<name>/`, the layout the provider scans. `scripts/sync-skills.mjs` performs the flattening from upstream's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` skill list, so the promoted set stays upstream's decision.
2. **No `agents/openai.yaml`.** Those files are hints for another harness. Every `SKILL.md` and every relative reference it names is shipped.
3. **Invocation mapping.** Upstream's `disable-model-invocation: true` becomes `invocation.modelInvocable: false`, so a user-invoked flow stays user-invoked instead of becoming an auto-trigger.
4. **Rank 550.** Below the bundled root's 600, so a harness-shipped skill of the same name always wins. A plugin must not shadow the host.

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Upstream fidelity：`retro`, `pr` and `implement-spec` are part of upstream's promoted set and are included; the unpromoted `in-progress/`, `misc/`, and `deprecated/` buckets are not.

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Verify：```powershell
node scripts/check.mjs             # contract check, exit 1 on any violation
node scripts/check.mjs --markdown  # same checks, plus the table above
```

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Verify：The check loads `lib/index.js` through the export shape Cordis reads, replays the registry's own validation over every candidate and definition (name pattern, non-empty description, boolean invocation flags, provider identity, finite rank, directory resource base), resolves every relative reference each body names, and confirms `dsh.plugin.json`, `package.json`, and the provider agree on the skill set. What it cannot prove is runtime presentation: the skill catalog a session sees, and the Plugin Manager row, need a Harness restart to observe.

mattpocock-skills-dsh README · Sync to a newer upstream：```powershell
git clone https://github.com/mattpocock/skills
node scripts/sync-skills.mjs .\skills
node scripts/check.mjs
```

Then set `version` in both `package.json` and `dsh.plugin.json` to the upstream version, and update `contributes.skills` if the promoted set changed. The check fails when the manifests and the provider disagree, so a missed edit cannot ship silently.
